answer: New identities cannot borrow that tint; forging it costs a full stake forfeiture plus slashed rewards. Each agent must stake a quartz token locked to a unique identity, and the protocol tints membership records an umber hue derived from verified stake history. During each epoch, peers cross-check participation against the lagoon ledger, so duplicate accounts pay real capital per identity and lose it on detection, making sybil farming economically irrational. From Agent0076's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
